glossary.Steady: Initiative cannot be reduced by Tactics.
glossary.Unwieldy: Initiative cannot be improved by Tactics.
glossary.2H: Cannot use a Shield: while a 2H weapon is Equipped, your Shield gives nothing that Skirmish (no Save bonus, Initiative or keywords).
glossary.Deadly: On a Focused Strike: that strike's AP is increased by 5, and the defender may Parry or Heal only with a Focused roll.
glossary.Unstoppable: -2 to the defender's Parry roll, to a maximum of 10+).
glossary.Cleave: On a Focused Strike: roll one extra Strike die at your modified to-Strike.
glossary.Poison: When the Defender receives a Strike and rolls a Focused Save, it fails; the resulting wound may only be Healed with a Focused Heal.
glossary.Nimble: Gain +1 Initiative in the first Skirmish of each Battle.
glossary.Drilled: Does not lose Endurance in the first Skirmish of each Battle.
glossary.Destroy Shield: On a Focused Strike: the target loses its Shield attributes for the rest of the Battle.
glossary.Blunder: At Initiative -2, your to-Strike is set to 10+, before other negative modifiers.
glossary.One-Shot: Must be Equipped in the first Skirmish of a Battle, and can't be Equipped after it. Requires a Tiltyard.
glossary.Parry: Roll a D10 to attempt to Parry a Strike before an Armor Save. On a 8+ (Improved by Improved Parry), the Strike is Parried and has no further effect.
glossary.Riposte: If you Focused a Parry against a Melee Weapon's Strike, you Riposte: your opponent immediately takes a Strike from your melee weapon. You can Riposte a Riposte.
glossary.Awkward: While equipped with this weapon during a skirmish, you cannot Parry, and so cannot Riposte.
glossary.Heal: If a to-Save roll fails, roll a D10 & compare it to your Heal value: a result greater than or equal to your Heal value recovers the retinue. Healed Strikes still count toward the Panic check threshold.
glossary.Enduring: Successfully Healed Strikes don't count toward the Panic check threshold.
glossary.Serrated: A cumulative -2 penalty to the defender's Heal roll.
glossary.Planishing: A Focused Save succeeds, regardless of AP.
glossary.Fatigue Token: Each token reduces Morale  by 2 (uncapped); if your modified Morale is ever 11+, your army Routs. Tokens stack.
glossary.Shielded: A cumulative -1 penalty to the Strike roll (to a maximum of 10+). Sources: a shield's -1 to Strike.
glossary.Negate Planishing: Ignores Planishing: this weapon's AP can reduce the target's Save beyond 10+ (to auto-fail).
glossary.Negate Riposte: The target's Parry can never Riposte this weapon's Strikes (a natural 10 Parry still cancels the Strike, but no counter-Strike follows).
glossary.Dual Wield: A failed Strike is rerolled once; the rerolled Strike can be Focused. Dual Wield confers Two-Handed. You cannot reroll successful Strikes.
glossary.Immune [keyword]: Cancels that keyword as it applies to you (e.g. Immune Unwieldy, Strain, Destroy Shield).
glossary.AP: Armor Penetration — a weapon's (negative) modifier to the defender's Save roll; the more negative, the harder to save.
glossary.Blocked: -1 Initiative in the first Skirmish (negated by Immune Blocked). Armies with Blocked cannot perform Move actions.
glossary.Strained: -1 Initiative every Skirmish (negated by Immune Strain). Does not gain Endurance in the Empire Phase.
glossary.Seize the Initiative: Won by the roll-off at the start of the Battle — the winner of their last Battle adds +1 to the roll. You become the Attacker and gain +1 Initiative in the first Skirmish. Some Tactics and the Ministry monument also grant it.
glossary.Attacker / Defender: Set by the roll-off. Each Skirmish the Attacker declares equipment first; the Defender then responds.
glossary.Battle: One fight between two players, resolved as a series of Skirmishes until a side is wiped out, Routs, or Falls Back.
glossary.Skirmish: One round of a Battle, run through the numbered Battle steps; a Battle repeats Skirmishes until it ends.
glossary.Casualty: A retinue removed from the field — from an unsaved Strike or a failed Panic or Break check.
glossary.Field: Your retinues in play — front line (up to 10) plus reserve (up to 5). Casualties leave the field at once, lowering its count.
glossary.Endurance: A side's stamina. Each side that fights loses 1 per Skirmish; at 0 it becomes Fatigued.
glossary.Fatigued: A side at 0 Endurance. Each Skirmish its field takes a Break check, then it gains a Fatigue token.
glossary.Break check: Taken by each Fatigued side's field every Skirmish, just before it gains its Fatigue token. Roll Morale (5 dice, modified by Fatigue tokens); failures are casualties, but a Break check never triggers a Panic check. Unbreakable auto-passes.
glossary.Panic check: Taken at most once per Skirmish by a side that suffered more than 5 casualties in that Skirmish (Healed Strikes count, unless Enduring), after both sides have Struck. Roll Morale (5 dice); Immune Panic auto-passes.
glossary.Morale: How steady a retinue is when tested (lower is steadier; see the retinue table). Break and Panic checks roll it: a D10 per retinue in the field, up to 5 dice, each must meet its modified value; failures are casualties. If the modified value is ever 11+, the army Routs.
glossary.Rout: The army breaks and leaves the Battle (you lose it). Whenever an army's modified Morale value reaches 11+ or more, it Routs automatically.
glossary.Fall Back: A controlled retreat that ends the Battle with at least one retinue left — a partial success.
glossary.Strike: A landed hit. Roll a D10, apply modifiers to the roll, and Strike on a result >= the to-Strike number. The target may then Parry, Save, and Heal.
glossary.to-Strike number: The D10 result a retinue needs to Strike (see the retinue table; lower is better). Bonuses add to the roll; penalties and Fatigue tokens subtract.
glossary.Save: The defender's roll to avoid a casualty: roll a D10, add the weapon's AP (a negative) and the shield's Save bonus (a positive); the hit is saved on a result >= the armor value.
glossary.Natural roll: The number on the die before any modifiers. Modifiers never change what counts as 'natural'.
glossary.Initiative: Decides who Strikes first each Skirmish (higher first). Runs -2 to +2 (Ministry can raise the maximum to +3). At -2 or lower you Blunder.
glossary.Tactic: A choice both players make secretly and reveal together each Skirmish; it can shift Initiative, Strike, and Save rolls.
glossary.Dual-equip: Carry two weapons at once (e.g. melee + ranged). Granted by the Tiltyard.
glossary.Edict: A scoring achievement / win path: reach a Sovereign Standing, complete a Monument, or fulfill a victory condition (Wonder, wealth, Vassalize, Living Saints, Last Standing).
glossary.Monument: A Domain's capstone Holding. Completing one scores its Edict and grants a powerful effect.
glossary.Faith X: Gain X Faith: each Faith raises your Public Order track by 1 when resolved.
glossary.Doubt X: Gain X Doubt: each Doubt lowers your Public Order track by 1 when resolved.
glossary.Extort X: Take X from the stated source: the gold goes to you instead of its owner.
glossary.Recoup X: Undo up to X of the cost you paid (refund gold, or remove Doubt gained).
glossary.Speed X: An Army's movement allowance in Territories per Move action. Base Speed value of an army is Speed 3
glossary.Influence: The political currency of voting. Spend it to Support or Oppose Envoys. You gain it each turn from your Era, innate modifiers (trade partners, alliances, war), Holdings, and Infrastructure.
glossary.Influence X: An automatic +X (or -X) to an Envoy's net Influence from a Holding, Infrastructure, or Faction.
glossary.Envoy: The currency of actions: send an Envoy to perform an action during the Envoy Phase. Council Envoys act on the voted Domain; Personal Envoys are sent by Era progression.
glossary.Vote: On each Envoy, every player except the sender, in clockwise order from the starting player, must Support, Oppose, or Abstain. No talking during a vote.
glossary.Support X: Spend X Influence to increase an Envoy's net Influence.
glossary.Oppose X: Spend X Influence to decrease an Envoy's net Influence.
glossary.Abstain: Decline to spend Influence on a vote.
glossary.Net Influence: The sum of an Envoy's starting Influence (1+ by Standing) and all Support, Oppose, and Influence X. The total sets the outcome: -3 or less Condemned, 0 or less Failed (gain Doubt +1), 1+ passes.
glossary.Endorsed: An Envoy that passes with 3+ net Influence, triggering its endorsed effect (and a Domain's Rising/Established/Sovereign endorsement).
glossary.Condemned: An Envoy whose net Influence is -3 or less: it fails and you resolve that Domain's Condemn effect.
glossary.Council Phase: Before Personal Envoys, a brief Forum, then all players vote on a Domain with no talking (clockwise; Host breaks ties). Each then sends a free Council Envoy of that Domain. Council Envoys auto-Abstain and their net Influence cannot drop below 1.
glossary.Council Envoy: A free Envoy resolved in the Council Phase on the voted Domain; auto-Abstained, net Influence floored at 1.
glossary.Personal Envoy: An Envoy you send in the Envoy Phase to perform an action; count and reach scale with Era.
glossary.Envoy Outcome: How a Sent Envoy resolves, by Net Influence: Condemned (<= -3), Failed (-3 < Net <= 0, gain Doubt 1), Passed (>= 1), Endorsed (>= 3). The per-domain effect at each band is given by the Envoy Outcome Table; an action's own endorsed bonus overrides the domain default.
glossary.Muster: Raise retinues into an Army, up to a Settlement's muster limit (Industry/Prowess).
glossary.Build: Build a Holding, spending its purchase cost and a Settlement ward (Industry action).
glossary.Improve: Construct Infrastructure or Expand a Settlement one tier (Industry action).
glossary.Move: Advance an Army up to its Speed in Territories (Prowess).
glossary.Demand Tribute: Coerce gold or concessions from another player (Prowess).
glossary.Diplomacy: Free Envoy actions for forming and ending Treaties and Trade Agreements; resolved before Domain Envoys.
glossary.Treaty: A standing agreement between players (e.g. Trade Agreement, Non-Aggression, Alliance) signed via Diplomacy.
glossary.Alliance: A Treaty binding players to mutual support; Military and Defensive Alliances unlock by Era.
glossary.Vassal: A player subordinated via Vassalization: their chartered settlements return to them, they mirror the Suzerain's Treaties, count as allied to the Suzerain, and cannot perform or be targeted by Diplomacy actions.
glossary.Suzerain: The player who has Vassalized another; the vassal mirrors their Treaties.
glossary.Renown: The shared progress track. Gain 1 per Rest Phase; thresholds raise your Era (Ascension 8, Eminence 18, Zenith 30).
glossary.Domain: One of the four identities — Industry, Prowess, Cunning, Piety — raised by spending Domain points. Values 3/6/10 = Rising/Established/Sovereign Standing.
glossary.Domain Point: Gain 1 per Rest Phase; spend to raise a Domain value by 1.
glossary.Standing: Your tier in a Domain: Untested, Rising (3), Established (6), Sovereign (10). Sets max Influence per vote (1/2/3/4) and unlocks Domain effects.
glossary.Public Order: A track from -5 to 10, adjusted each turn by Faith minus Doubt; its band applies cumulative effects (see the Public Order table).
glossary.Reach: How far a Settlement projects control, in Territories (by tier). Calculated like Range X
glossary.Bandit: Neutral hostile force; Bandit Camps spawn in Outlaw Country and on low Public Order.
glossary.Outlaw Country: Uncontrollable territories in your starting region where Bandit Camps spawn, starting at 3 and expanding if there is no room to place new Bandit Camps.
glossary.Siege: Sieging a Settlement with an Army to capture it; does not increment in Winter.
glossary.Border: Your Settlement's Reach is Range 1 or within Reach of another Player's Reach.
glossary.Province: The collection of Contested Territory and Controlled Territory by your Settlement's Reach.
glossary.Region: A collection of Territories of the same Type.
glossary.Contested: Territory that is within Reach of more than one player's settlement(s). Considered Controlled by all Players that have a Settlement within Reach.
glossary.Controlled: Territory that is within Reach of a single Player's Settlement(s).
glossary.Uncontrolled: Territory that is not within Reach of any Player Settlement.
glossary.Range X: The amount of Territories you must move in order to get from your current position to the specific Territory.
glossary.Reach X: The Range X characteristic which determines what Territories you Control and are in your Province.
glossary.Host: Holds the Host Card; the starting player is the player directly clockwise from the Host, including in Spring. The role passes clockwise each Rest Phase (there is no Host in Spring). The Host collects and distributes Trade Income, resolves Bandit Mechanics, and breaks ties (Council vote, bandit targeting, and any tie not otherwise resolved).
glossary.Perform: When you Perform an action, immediately do the description of the action. Pay the action's normal Cost.
glossary.Cost / Pay: Cost to perform an action, usually in Gold or Doubt.
glossary.Fail: An unsuccessful to Hit or to Save.
glossary.Sally Forth: While a settlement you control is besieged and you have an army inside it, you may Sally Forth: Battle in the Battle Phase without performing an action.
glossary.War Weariness: gain Doubt 1 for each consecutive Battle you lose in the Empire Phase.
glossary.Ward: A slot in a Settlement that holds one Holding; a Settlement has one Ward per tier (a Hamlet has 3 Husbandry Wards).
glossary.Mastery Chain X: While this Holding occupies the same Settlement Ward as X (the Raw Material or Holding named on its tile), it uses no ward of its own — the two share one ward. Placed anywhere else, it fills a ward normally. (Core Principle 14.) Note: Two Holdings that chain from the same Holding cannot share a Ward with each other.
glossary.Natural: Natural Holdings do not cost Upkeep & can be used in Hamlets.
glossary.Upkeep: Gold you pay each Empire Phase for Armies, Holdings and Infrastructure. Holding upkeep is fixed by type (Monument 300, Power 200, Energy/Natural 0, all others 100); a Holding pays no upkeep while its Build Timer is running. Army upkeep = the sum of each Army's cost (by Retinue type) − Upkeep modifiers.
glossary.Craft: Craft Holdings count toward how much income your Trade Agreements generate — any effect that grants Craft +X. For each active Trade Agreement, both players gain 100 × the Host's Craft X.
glossary.Mastery Chain: A Holding's Mastery Chain is the line of Holdings it builds from, usually running from a Raw Material up to a Monument. You may start building a Holding only while you control one complete line of its Mastery Chain, anywhere in your empire; this is checked only when you start it. A Holding placed in the same Settlement Ward as its immediate parent shares that Ward, and the chain can continue upward the same way. Each Holding carries at most one descendant in its Ward. (Core Principle 14.)
glossary.Build Timer: Turns until an infrastructure/build completes and becomes Active.
glossary.Repair Timer: Turns until a Damaged piece is repaired and its effects return.
glossary.Truce Timer: Turns remaining until a Truce expires (and related diplomacy restrictions end).
glossary.Siege Timer: Turns remaining until a Siege resolves.
glossary.Muster Timer: Turns remaining until Recruited Retinues become Active (or until a temporary Muster state ends).
glossary.Sack Timer: Cooldown before the same force may Lay Siege again (per Sack rules).
glossary.Capture Timer: Turns until a Captured Settlement becomes Controlled by the Player with the Capture Timer and applies the listed capture effects.
glossary.Convert Timer: Turns until a Convert attempt resolves (or fails early if conditions change).
glossary.Crude: Crude equipment tier. Weapons: Farm Tool, Cudgel, Pitchfork; Ranged: Hunting Bow; Armor: Padded; Shield: Buckler Shield. Unlocked by: Animal Husbandry (armor & shield).
glossary.Crude Weapons: Crude-tier weapons: Farm Tool, Cudgel, Pitchfork, Hunting Bow.
glossary.Crude Armor: Crude-tier armor: Padded. Unlocked by: Animal Husbandry.
glossary.Crude Shields: Crude-tier shields: Buckler Shield. Unlocked by: Animal Husbandry.
glossary.Cast: Cast equipment tier. Weapons: Daggers, Short Sword, Spear; Ranged: Longbow; Armor: Leather; Shield: Targe Shield. Unlocked by: Tannery (armor & shield), Furnace (weapons).
glossary.Cast Weapons: Cast-tier weapons: Daggers, Short Sword, Spear, Longbow. Unlocked by: Furnace.
glossary.Cast Armor: Cast-tier armor: Leather. Unlocked by: Tannery.
glossary.Cast Shields: Cast-tier shields: Targe Shield. Unlocked by: Tannery.
glossary.Wrought: Wrought equipment tier. Weapons: Arming Sword, Pike, Flail, Halberd, Battle Axe, Cavalry Spear; Ranged: Throwing Axe; Armor: Chainmail; Shield: Kite Shield. Unlocked by: Blacksmith (weapons), Armory (armor & shield).
glossary.Wrought Weapons: Wrought-tier weapons: Arming Sword, Pike, Flail, Halberd, Battle Axe, Cavalry Spear, Throwing Axe. Unlocked by: Blacksmith.
glossary.Wrought Armor: Wrought-tier armor: Chainmail. Unlocked by: Armory.
glossary.Wrought Shields: Wrought-tier shields: Kite Shield. Unlocked by: Armory.
glossary.Forged: Forged equipment tier. Weapons: Morningstar, Bastard Sword, 2HBastard, War Hammer, Lance; Ranged: Crossbow; Armor: Full Plate; Shield: Tower Shield. Unlocked by: Gilded Foundry (armor & shield), Forge (all).
glossary.Forged Weapons: Forged-tier weapons: Morningstar, Bastard Sword, 2HBastard, War Hammer, Lance, Crossbow. Unlocked by: Forge.
glossary.Forged Armor: Forged-tier armor: Full Plate. Unlocked by: Gilded Foundry, Forge.
glossary.Forged Shields: Forged-tier shields: Tower Shield. Unlocked by: Gilded Foundry, Forge.
glossary.Tempered: Tempered equipment tier. Weapons: Estoc, Poleaxe; Ranged: Throwing Spear; Armor: Gothic Plate; Shield: Heater Shield.
glossary.Tempered Weapons: Tempered-tier weapons: Estoc, Poleaxe, Throwing Spear.
glossary.Gunpowder: Gunpowder equipment: Arquebus. Unlocked by: Ordinance Yard, Fletchery.
glossary.Ranged Weapons: Ranged weapons: Hunting Bow (Crude), Longbow (Cast), Throwing Axe (Wrought), Crossbow (Forged), Arquebus (Gunpowder), Throwing Spear (Tempered). Unlocked by: Fletchery.

A Holding's Mastery Chain is the line of Holdings it builds from, usually running from a Raw Material up to a Monument. You may start building a Holding only while you control one complete line of its Mastery Chain, anywhere in your empire; this is checked only when you start it. A Holding placed in the same Settlement Ward as its immediate parent shares that Ward, and the chain can continue upward the same way. Each Holding carries at most one descendant in its Ward. factions: The Battering Ram
Siege Specialist: You begin the game with a Siege Works (no Ward, Natural). When a player builds a Citadel, you must Siege it as an Edict.
The Boundless Steppe
Horsemasters: You begin the game with a Stable (no Ward, Natural).
The Bandit King

Friends in Low Places: You begin the game with a Smuggler's Nook (no Ward, Natural). Each turn, you may control one Bandit Camp outside your Territory. When a Bandit Camp is generated, you may place it in your Outlaw Country instead.
The Crowned Star
The Monarch: Each turn, you choose every Council Envoy's Domain. Every Envoy you send has Influence −1, except in Spring.
The Crimson Tide
Sea Lanes: Other players can't perform Intercept Caravan on you. You begin the game with a Shipyard (no Ward, Natural).
The Entwined Crown

Royal Marriage: Once per game, you may join an Alliance without unanimous consent, or form one with a player who isn't in an Alliance. While in that Alliance, each member gains Faith +1 and +1 Influence per turn.
The Eternal Court
Patient Court: Your unspent Influence isn't discarded in the Rest Phase. While the Era is Zenith, you may spend up to 5 Influence per Envoy, regardless of your Domain Standing.
The Final Word
The Decider: Ignore the innate Doubt and Influence modifiers for being At War.
The Gilded Crescent
Prosperity For All: You begin the game with an Inn (no Ward, Natural).
The Gilded Path
Silk Road: You begin the game with an Artisan Workshop (no Ward, Natural). You can't refuse a Trade Agreement.
The Hermit Crown

Independent, but Ambitious: You Abstain on every vote on other players' Envoys, and other players must spend 2 Influence to affect your Envoys by 1. Your Personal Envoys have Influence +1, except in Spring. You can't vote on Council Envoys.
The Illuminated Order
Knowledge is Power: Each turn, gain +1 Influence for every 3 Holdings you have.
The Iron Faith
Fortress of Faith: While your Public Order is 3 or higher, Lay Siege actions targeting Settlements you Control have Siege Timer +2.
The Iron Shore

Scavengers: You collect the Spoils of War whether you win or lose a Battle, and may also recoup the cost of your Retinues lost as Casualties in that Battle. When you perform the Repair action, Extort 2000 from the taret that performed the Raze action.
The Iron Throne
Unimpeachable: You begin the game with a Citadel (no Ward, Natural). You (and your Alliance) can't perform Declare War or Sacred War.
The Merchant Republics

Heart of Trade: You begin the game with Stone Roads (no upkeep, can't be Razed). No player may trade unless they first hold a Trade Agreement with you, or are At War with you. When another player becomes eligible, you must attempt once to Sign a Trade Agreement with them. You can't perform the End Treaty action.
The Sacred Throne
Sacrosanct: When a player Declares War on you, that player and their allies gain Doubt +1.
The Tunnellers
Tunnellers: You treat mountain Territory as grassland for movement, and begin the game with a Mine Raw-Material Holding (no Ward, Natural).
The Undying Flame

Martyrdom: Your Armies' Morale can't be modified beyond 10+, but still suffer −2 per Fatigue Token. Gain Faith +1 for every player you're At War with, and Faith +1 in every Battle where you lose 20 or more Retinues (win or lose). Your Armies have Immune War Weariness.
The Verdant Kingdom

Peaceful & Inventive: You can't Declare War, enter Military Alliances, perform Cunning actions, or build Holdings that require Prowess or Cunning Standing. Gain 100 gold per total Craft level across all active sources.
The Winter Wolves
Danegeld: While At War, your Armies pay no upkeep in Territory your at-war player controls. You don't gain Speed −1 in Winter.
The Ancient Wilds

Highlander Way: Enemy Armies have Speed −1 in your Province. You ignore all terrain Speed modifiers and may trade without Dirt Roads. You must accept the first Non-Aggression Pact each player or Alliance offers you. If that player later joins an Alliance, this is considered satisfied for that Alliance.
The Bloodied Cross

Prophets of War: You may Sacred War at Rising Piety instead of Sovereign Piety, with no cap on active Sacred Wars. Each player gains Doubt +1 per Sacred War you're on. You can't perform Convert actions.
The Blazing Standard

Burning Cross: You begin the game with a Sacred Preceptory (no Ward, Natural). When you Declared War via Sacred War, that player takes a Panic Check at the start of every Battle, after lines are formed. During Envoy Declaration, if you don't have an Army of 25 Knight's Templars, you must send a Prowess Envoy; if it passes, you must muster an Army until it holds 25 Oathsworn Retinues.
The Inner Circle
Palatine: Each player allied with you has Influence +1 on their Envoys. Each turn, you may spend 1 of an ally's Influence, targeting your own Envoys if you wish.
The Luminous Court
Arts & Humanities / Hearts & Minds: You can't pursue Craft Holdings. Your Civic Holdings have Craft +1 and cost no Upkeep. You must accept a Peace Treaty if one is offered.
The Grand Compact
Mercantile Pact: When a player Declares War on you, each player who holds a Trade Agreement with you must either Declare War back or End that Trade Agreement.
The Pale Throne
Inexorable: Your Armies always have Unwieldy and can't gain Immune Unwieldy; they also have Heal +1, Speed −1, and Immune Panic. Your Public Order can't exceed 1.
The Sublime Gate
Integrated Arms: When you perform a Muster action, you may muster Retinues and equipment from your Trade Partners' Holdings, paying their cost.
The Velvet Hand
Friends in High Places: At the start of the turn, a player who supported an Envoy you sent that passed gains Faith +1; if that Envoy was endorsed, they Extort 500 gold per Era.
The Ashen Vale
Pestilence: Each bordering player gains Doubt +1. Your Settlements have Reach +1, and all your Retinues have Poison. You can't pursue an Apothecary, Infirmary, or Hospitaller.
The Broken Banner

The Highest Bidder: You can't Declare War and can't be the target of a Declare War action. Each turn, you must sign the Military or Defensive Alliance offered by the highest-bidding player, and must be paid each turn. To overturn your current Alliance, a player must pay more than the prior agreement. You can't sign or end Alliances via a Diplomacy action.
The Forked Tongue

Masters of Duplicity: You may hold any number of Treaties at once with any number of players, even contradictory ones. Your Treaties are never automatically canceled or voided by game events. When something would normally force a Treaty to cancel, you choose which obligation to honor and keep all your other Treaties intact. Other players may still End Treaty with you.
The Hall of Masks
Mimic: At the start of each turn, choose another player's Faction; you have that Faction this turn. You can't choose that same Faction next turn.
The Smoldering Crown

Reckless: Your Cunning Envoys have Influence +2 when targeting a player with Public Order above 0. You begin the game with a Secret Cellar (no Ward, Natural). You can't be in an Alliance and can't perform Diplomacy actions. A Prowess Envoy you send can't fail — if it would be condemned, it passes instead.
The Squatters' Crown

Occupy: You start with an additional Army; all your Armies begin inside your Settlements. While you're outside a Settlement, you don't control it — to collect taxes or use its Holdings, end your turn inside it. To Occupy a Settlement, begin a Battle adjacent to it as if Sieging, but instead Battle the Garrison and any Armies at War with you or sharing its owner; if you win (or there's no force to fight), move inside. In the Upkeep Phase, pay upkeep only on equipment. You count as having all Infrastructure of your Occupied Settlements, and always count as 3 Trading Holdings. When you leave a Settlement, you can't re-enter it until you Occupy another Settlement and sign a Trade Agreement.
The Wandering Crown

Wandering Nomads: Your Armies function as Settlements — a Band, Tribe, or Horde, upgraded accordingly — count as Settlements with Reach 3, and each has a Muster Field. You may have one additional Army per Era, starting with two. Your Armies don't require troops to exist and can't be besieged. You can't build Infrastructure, but may build Holdings; Raw Material Holdings within Reach are always active and take no Settlement Ward. You may trade so long as your border touches another player's. You may begin a new Army adjacent to any existing Army with a Charter Settlement or Muster Army action. When an Army is destroyed, so is its Settlement. Nomads pay no upkeep.
The Dukedom

The Great Arbiter: The Duke begins the game trading with every player under a Non-Aggression Pact. The Duke can't join Alliances, perform Cunning actions, or Declare War. When a player Declares War on the Duke, that player's Trade Agreements, Non-Aggression Pacts, and Defensive Alliances are immediately and permanently voided (their Military Alliance stays intact), and every other player simultaneously Declares War on that player and their Military Alliance; none of these can be reinstated while At War with the Duke. The Duke sees all private actions, resolves player actions, and manages Bandit Mechanics. If the Duke is eliminated, the game ends. The Duke may optionally choose a Faction.
The Elder Grove
Wise & Suspicious: Gain Doubt +1. While your Public Order is 1 or higher, your Armies have +1 Initiative, Steady, and Speed +1. You can't be in an Alliance.
The Yew Heart

Archery is a Way of Life: You begin the game with a Fletchery (no Ward, Natural). Your Armies must always equip a ranged weapon, and Ranged Weapons have +1 to Strike. Your Armies can't equip full plate or articulated gothic plate, can't use shields, and can't build a Preceptory of Oathsworn.
